title: VEFTA: Can Vietnamese businesses turn market access into gains?
summary:
Vietnam’s new EFTA free trade agreement, signed on October 18, 2026, offers exporters wider access to Switzerland, Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein but hinges on business readiness.
Textile, garment and footwear firms’ reliance on imported raw materials could hinder rules-of-origin compliance and tariff use.
SMEs face finance, technology, traceability and environmental compliance gaps.

title: Global export curbs cover a record $1.5 trn by end-June 2026: WTO
summary:
WTO says import-related restrictive and non-facilitating measures introduced since 2009 and still in force covered $5.4 trillion, or 21.3 per cent of world imports, as of June 30, 2026. 
WTO members and observers recorded 1,048 trade-related measures in Jan-June 2026 after 1,229 in 2025. 
Facilitating steps also rose to 466 in six months, but 333 new restrictive measures exceeded 2025's total.

title: US trade groups urge PMA & ILWU Local 26 to keep cargo moving
summary:
More than 110 US trade associations have urged the Pacific Maritime Association and ILWU Local 26 to keep negotiating, move cargo and avoid a strike or disruption at Los Angeles and Long Beach ports. 
They warned a stoppage could endanger holiday retail shipments, halt exports and restrict components for manufacturers. 
The ports already face congestion from near-record import volumes.

title: China & Canada sign financial working group terms
summary:
China’s central bank has signed terms for the China-Canada Financial Working Group with Canada’s Department of Finance and the Bank of Canada. 
The framework sets participants, cooperation areas and communication methods to support regular operation of the group. 
Its agenda includes currency swap use, local currencies in bilateral trade and investment, green finance and payments.

title: EU bans plastic waste exports to non-OECD countries
summary:
EU exports of plastic waste to non-OECD countries will be prohibited from November 21, 2026 under the Waste Shipment Regulation. 
The ban applies until at least May 21, 2029; OECD-bound exports remain possible under greater scrutiny. 
The EU generates around 40 million tonnes of plastic waste yearly and exported 1-1.5 million tonnes annually, the Commission said.

title: IEA sees Hormuz crisis accelerating shift towards electricity
summary:
The Hormuz crisis is prompting countries to diversify supplies, develop domestic energy resources and accelerate electrification, as per the IEA. 
Prolonged disruption could sharply reduce oil flows through the strait, while a resolution could ease oil and gas prices. 
Solar and nuclear power stand to gain, but higher fuel costs threaten progress on energy access in developing economies.

title: OECD growth slows to 0.6% in Q3 2026 as major economies diverge
summary:
GDP growth across the OECD area slowed to 0.6 per cent quarter-on-quarter in Q3 2026 from 0.7 per cent in the previous quarter, while G7 growth remained unchanged at 0.5 per cent. 
Growth accelerated in the US and UK but slowed in Canada and Germany, while Japan and Italy stagnated and France contracted. 
EU and euro area growth also eased to 0.5 per cent and 0.4 per cent, respectively, the OECD said.

title: Euro area's LEI slips to 102.5 in October
summary:
Euro area's LEI fell 0.1 per cent in October 2026 to 102.5, its fifth decline in seven months, with The Conference Board saying the six-month growth rate remained negative.
The index dropped 0.8 per cent over the six months to October; the CEI was unchanged at 110.2.
Consumer expectations were the main drag, while inflation reached 4.0 per cent year on year and energy prices rose 20.8 per cent.

title: ₹23,000cr funding push: Can India lift export competitiveness in 2027?
summary:
India seeks RoDTEP and RoSCTL extensions beyond December 31, with ₹23,000 crore (~$2.46 billion) sought for RoDTEP.
Budget allocations fall to ₹10,000 crore and ₹5,000 crore, respectively; an Export Promotion Mission merger is proposed.
US-bound RoSCTL shipments fell 19.4 per cent to $4.14 billion in January–July 2026, accounting for 88 per cent of the segment’s decline.

title: Lyocell prices split: China weakens, India firms on cost support
summary:
Lyocell staple fibre diverged across Asia over three weeks, with India rising and China slipping as the India-China price gap widened by about 28 per cent.
Chinese offers moved from $2.131/kg to $2.121/kg, while Indian prices climbed from $2.293/kg to $2.328/kg.
Dissolving pulp stayed flat, leaving China with a thinner fibre-over-pulp spread.

title: Bangladesh leads EU denim market as exports fall 5.48% in Jan-Sep
summary:
Bangladesh remained the EU’s largest denim supplier in January–September 2026, accounting for 29.48 per cent of imports. 
EU purchases from Bangladesh fell 5.48 per cent year on year to €1.01 billion, outpacing the 3.24 per cent decline in overall denim imports. 
In September alone, shipments from Bangladesh rose 0.70 per cent YoY to €143 million.

title: New Zealand's apparel imports rise 12% YoY in October 2026
summary:
New Zealand’s apparel imports rose 12 per cent to NZ$189.24 million (~$103.98 million) in October 2026, marking a fourth consecutive monthly gain.
Both knitted and non-knitted apparel posted double-digit growth, while exports recovered by 6 per cent.
However, modest January-October growth and weaker cumulative non-knitted apparel exports showed that the clothing trade recovery remained uneven overall.

title: Can South Africa’s apparel manufacturers stay competitive?
summary:
Levi Strauss has proposed closing its Epping facility in Cape Town, putting more than 400 jobs at risk, as per reports.
The company has begun Section 189 consultations under South Africa’s Labour Relations Act and says no final decision will be made before talks end.
AGOA uncertainty, rising costs and underused capacity are cited as pressures on local clothing and textile competitiveness.

title: Bangladesh's RMG unrest causes daily losses of up to $176 mn: BGBA
summary:
Bangladesh is losing Tk 2,000-2,200 crore (~$160-176 million) in daily output due to RMG production disruption, BGBA has said.
It put cumulative losses from factory closures and road blockades at Tk 3,000-4,000 crore (~$240-320 million).
The association warned export shipments, buyer confidence, future orders and factory operations could be hit unless the wage dispute is resolved.

title: China's share of Singapore's apparel imports rises to 33%
summary:
Singapore’s apparel imports rose 7.4 per cent to $1.562 billion in January–September 2026, reversing the recent decline.
China strengthened its lead, with shipments up 16.9 per cent to $517.984 million and share rising to 33.17 per cent.
Italy remained second, Vietnam gained, while Indonesia and Malaysia lost ground; knitted apparel led the import basket.

title: 26% of Canada's apparel imports: What's at stake by 2032?
summary:
Bangladesh's LDC graduation has been deferred to November 2029, which could extend Canada's duty-free apparel access until November 2032.
Cambodia could retain similar benefits until December 2032; the two accounted for about 26 per cent of Canada's apparel imports by value in 2025.
Without LDCT or another preference, high-volume garments face MFN duties of 17-18 per cent, raising sourcing risk.

title: US' Gap Inc appoints Ashley Kechter as Athleta CEO from December 14
summary:
Gap Inc has appointed Ashley Kechter as brand president and chief executive officer of Athleta, effective December 14, reporting to president and CEO Richard Dickson.
Kechter joins from Vuori, where she was global president, and has also led Fabletics.
Her experience spans apparel, activewear, sourcing, supply chain, merchandising and international expansion.

title: Cambodia's $10.22 bn apparel exports: Can growth last into 2027?
summary:
Cambodia’s apparel exports reached a record $10.22 billion in January-October 2026, up 6.31 per cent year on year; garments accounted for 34.1 per cent of merchandise shipments.
Knitted apparel rose 4.3 per cent and woven apparel 10.9 per cent, while shipments to the US rose as its apparel imports fell.
Imported fabric dependence and US tariff rules pose risks for buyers and manufacturers.

title: Bangladesh plans $3.5 mn post-LDC trade push
summary:
Bangladesh plans a $3.5 million, three-year push to strengthen trade competitiveness after least developed country graduation, according to the commerce ministry. 
About $2.5 million is proposed for seven priority areas in the WTO's EIF Phase Three project. 
Areas cover AI market forecasts, processed food, geographical indication goods, trade facilitation, ESG, carbon markets and negotiation training.

title: Bangladesh's CPD proposes new pay benchmarks for RMG workers
summary:
Bangladesh's CPD has proposed a monthly minimum wage of Tk18,578 (~$149) to Tk24,204 (~$195) for RMG workers, ahead of a new wage due on December 1.
Its benchmarks cover inflation, the urban Dhaka poverty line and a living-wage basket for a four-member household with 1.58 earners.
The wage board meets on November 23; workers seek Tk32,000 (~$257), while owners have not filed a proposal.
